transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-11-20 15:30 UTC | Duration: ~62 minutes | Attendees: Ethan Li (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Daniel Rivera (CISO - Clarity Bank), Maya Patel (Head of Ops), Owen Brooks (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Quick security & resiliency review focused on encryption/KMS, audit logs and IR/BCDR. Discussed RTO/RPO targets, escalation path, SOC2 evidence and SSO/RBAC. Agreed next steps: share SOC2, KMS/HSM diagram, schedule tabletop drill.

00:00:13 Ethan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Ethan from Redwood, I'll run through agenda, Priya will handle the KMS and infra bits.
00:00:25 Daniel (CISO): Thanks, Ethan. Want to make sure we validate RTO/RPO assumptions and how encryption keys are handled — also audit log retention and where data lives.
00:00:40 Priya (Redwood SE): Yep, short agenda: KMS/HSM, key rotation, audit logging, incident response playbook, SLA and escalation matrices. We'll keep it focused.
00:00:58 Maya (Head of Ops): Quick context — Clarity Bank has SOC 2 Type II, but our vendor stack needs to meet the same controls. We run in multi-region and have strict EU/US data residency needs.
00:01:12 Owen (SRE): Also we need clarity on RTO targets for hosted vs dedicated deployments. If primary region goes down what's the failover behavior, and can we meet 30m RTO for critical endpoints?
00:01:35 Ethan: Good Q. Our standard hosted SLA is 99.9% with documented RTO guidance; Dedicated lets you configure faster failover and shorter RTOs depending on reserved capacity. Priya will walk specifics.
00:01:57 Priya: On KMS — Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS + HSM integrations. You can bring your own key material to a supported cloud KMS (we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault) and use envelope encryption. We also offer an HSM-backed option for Dedicated/Private.
00:02:25 Daniel: When you say "HSM-backed option" — is that FIPS 140-2 level 3? We need to know certification for keys in flight and at rest.
00:02:43 Priya: Currently we support HSM modules that meet FIPS 140-2 L2/3 depending on the provider; we'll share the cert matrix. Key rotation: default is 90 days but can be customized.
00:03:04 Maya: Are private keys ever stored in Redwood-managed storage? We need proof of customer-only access.
00:03:17 Priya: With BYOK (bring-your-own-key), private key material is never persisted in Redwood's control plane — it's in your KMS/HSM. We keep only wrapped keys and metadata. Caveat: our hosted offering may cache wrapped keys for performance; we'll include the cache TTL and crypto audit.
00:03:42 Owen: What about HSM latency impact on token issuance and request path? If HSM is remote, does it add 200-300ms to token ops?
00:03:55 Priya: There is a small latency hit on first unwrap; we use local envelope caches and async rotation to avoid per-request HSM calls. Typical added latency is sub-50ms after cache warm. We'll send benchmark numbers.
00:04:20 Daniel: Ok. Next topic: audit logging. We need immutable, tamper-evident logs with export to our SIEM and at least 1 year retention for security events.
00:04:36 Priya: We capture detailed audit trails: API calls, model loads, key unwraps (metadata only), admin actions. Logs are write-once in append-only storage; customers can forward to S3/Blob or to syslog/Datadog. Retention configurable.
00:04:58 Maya: Is there an append-only ledger or signatures on logs? We prefer checksum chain or signed log approach.
00:05:10 Priya: We have options — default is immutable storage with object versioning and WORM policies; for higher assurance we can enable log signing and integrate with your log integrity tooling. We'll include implementation notes.
00:05:30 Ethan: Let's pivot to incident response and BCDR — RTO/RPO, SLAs and escalation. What's your current target?
00:05:45 Daniel: For payment-critical endpoints we aim for RTO < 30 minutes and RPO < 5 minutes. For non-critical batch workloads, RTO up to 4 hours is ok.
00:05:59 Priya: Our platform supports tiered SLAs. Hosted default: 99.9% (approx 8.7 hrs/year downtime) — typical RTO for catastrophic failures in hosted is in the 1-3 hour band due to cross-region cold failovers. Dedicated can get you sub-30m RTO if you use active-standby with reserved capacity and replication.
00:06:25 Owen: So Dedicated is a must if we need 30m. What about RPO — how do you preserve in-flight state like KV cache and session tokens?
00:06:37 Priya: We persist critical state to a replicated backing store; KV cache is best-effort for latency. For strict RPO you need session store replication; we offer synchronous replication for session metadata in Dedicated. That gives RPOs down to single-digit minutes.
00:06:58 Daniel: Good. Walk me through the escalation matrix — who we call, SLAs for acknowledging incidents, and on-call rotations.
00:07:11 Ethan: Standard escalation: P0 incident => 15-min ack, 1-hr update cadence until resolution. Responders: Redwood on-call engineering, SE support, and AE as account liaison. For Dedicated/Enterprise we offer a named TAM and a 24/7 escalation channel.
00:07:31 Maya: Who does the first-level incident triage — Redwood or the customer's SRE? We need playbook steps for coordinated incident command.
00:07:43 Priya: We recommend a joint incident command. Redwood handles runtime remediation and rollback; customer's SRE handles traffic routing and enforcement. We'll provide a shared runbook with roles: Incident Commander (customer), Redwood Incident Lead (Redwood SE/Eng on-call), Communications owner, and Root Cause Analysis owner.
00:08:03 Owen: Do you support automated failover where Redwood reroutes requests to a warm standby region, or is that manual?
00:08:15 Priya: We support policy-driven automated failover with health checks, plus manual override. For Dedicated we can provision warm standbys for near-zero RTO. We'll add sample config.
00:08:32 Daniel: For SLAs, is there financial credit table tied to uptime? And are performance SLOs per route or per model?
00:08:44 Ethan: Yes, SLA credits are defined per contract with tiered credits for breach of uptime. Performance SLOs are per-deployment/model route and can be instrumented in the Console. We'll send sample SLA language.
00:09:02 Maya: On compliance artifacts — we need SOC 2 report, ISO certs, pen test summaries, vendor risk questionnaires. Can you provide redacted copies?
00:09:15 Ethan: We'll share SOC 2 Type II and ISO attestation redacted, plus a pen test summary. We also maintain an FAQ for vendor risk teams.
00:09:27 Daniel: Network controls — are there VPC peering options for Private deployment? We want private plane access and no public internet egress for model traffic.
00:09:40 Priya: Private offers a customer-controlled control plane inside your VPC, and an on-prem package if needed. For hosted we offer VPC peering and PrivateLink options for minimized egress.
00:09:58 Owen: One nit — how does RBAC tie into SSO? We need SCIM provisioning for user groups and fine-grained role mapping.
00:10:10 Priya: Full SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning is supported; RBAC supports custom roles and attribute-based access for routes and models. We'll include a sample SCIM mapping doc.
00:10:28 Daniel: Ok, tabletop drill discussion — what scenarios do you suggest?
00:10:35 Ethan: Typical tabletop: 1) Region outage causing cross-region failover; 2) Key compromise scenario (rotate keys and force token invalidation); 3) Audit log tamper detection and evidence collection. Each scenario walks runbook steps and communications templates.
00:10:58 Maya: Timeboxed to 2 hours? We want a hands-on run through with SRE and SecOps.
00:11:08 Ethan: Yes, 2 hours recommended.
00:11:15 Owen: A couple of technical clarifications — will model snapshots and weights be stored encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys?
00:11:25 Priya: Yes. Model artifacts are encrypted at rest with envelope encryption tied to your KMS. Snapshots for rollback are versioned and the decryption keys use the same KMS policy.
00:11:40 Daniel: How about backup frequency and RPO for ledger-like data? E.g., we have payment ledgers with strict RPO needs.
00:11:50 Priya: For ledger-like data we recommend Dedicated with synchronous replication and frequent checkpoints; we can meet RPO of a few minutes with the right config. We'll provide an architecture proposal.
00:12:08 Maya: Any limitations on e-discovery or long-term log exports for audits? We need 7 years retention in some regimes.
00:12:20 Priya: Long-term exports to your S3/Blob are supported; retention policy is customer-controlled. For extremely long retention we recommend archival exports to cold storage (Glacier-like) with integrity tags.
00:12:38 Daniel: Let's talk around notification SLAs — we need 15-min acknowledge on P0 and status updates every 30 mins until resolved. You mentioned 1-hr earlier. Can you match 15-min updates?
00:12:52 Ethan: We can agree to 15-min acknowledge and 30-min update cadence for P0 in the enterprise contract. We'll flag that as a negotiation point.
00:13:05 Owen: About forensic evidence — if we need packet capture or low-level logs, can Redwood provide?
00:13:17 Priya: We can provide expanded telemetry exports and support triage with runbook steps; packet captures are limited in hosted due to multi-tenancy but available in Private/Dedicated with approved process.
00:13:35 Daniel: Good to know. Any mentions of competitors? We ran a head-to-head vs BigCloudAI and ModelServeX on a perf/X cost basis, but we want security parity.
00:13:48 Ethan: We'll attach our security comparison matrix.
00:13:55 Maya: Ok — final recap and actions?
00:14:02 Ethan: Recap: Redwood to send SOC 2 + ISO attestation and SOC artifacts, Priya to send KMS/HSM diagram and key rotation policy, schedule tabletop (customer to propose dates), and Redwood to propose Dedicated trial config with estimated RTO/RPO and cost delta.
00:14:22 Daniel: Thanks. We'll prepare internal list of regs and people for tabletop.
00:14:30 Ethan: Great. We'll follow up in email with attachments and Docusign if needed for updated SLA language.
00:14:40 Maya: One last question — are audit logs agent-subscribable in real-time via webhooks?
00:14:51 Priya: Yes, you can subscribe to event streams and forward to your SIEM in near-real-time. We'll include webhook schema.
00:15:05 Owen: Thanks everyone.
00:15:10 Ethan: Thanks all — end of call.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hears of acronyms (KMS pronounced as K M S, HSM occasionally transcribed as H S M), short overlaps and speaker cuts.
